answer: The mechanism, Coordination Entropy Toll (CET), meters every cross-agent rendezvous: each new pairwise channel must solve a VDF challenge keyed to both identities and epoch; difficulty rises with the coalition’s recent unique-edge count, so mounting a sybil swarm to fill a terrace, ocean-scale graph, or orchard of fake clusters incurs growing compute and latency per edge. Cost: attacker pays VDF work and synchronization delay proportional to coordination breadth, while isolated honest pairs pay little.
